 What Ohio's minimum wage increase will mean for businesses, employees
 Published October 20, 2026 at 4:01 AM EDT
 Listen • 25:22
 Alexander Grey 
 / 
 Unsplash 
 In 2006, Ohio voters passed a constitutional amendment to increase the minimum wage each year on Jan. 1 by the rate of inflation.
 In Jan. 2027, the minimum wage will increase to $11.40 per hour for non-tipped workers and $5.70 per hour for tipped employees, which represents a 3.5% increase.
 On Cincinnati Edition , we discuss what this increase might mean for businesses and workers and how Ohio is keeping up with inflation in comparison to other states.
 Guests:
 Michael Jones, Ph.D., associate professor of economics, University of Cincinnati
 Paul Sonn, senior policy expert for wages and affordability, National Employment Law Project
 Beginning at noon, call 513-419-7100 or email talk@wvxu.org to have your voice heard on this topic. You can catch a recorded replay at 8 p.m.
